problem: B12b product code, Quick evidence and control-plane verification converged, but its two human review evidence files were later deleted while the closed contract retained their historical SHA-256 values.

options.name: Recreate files and claim the old hashes
options.correctness: Impossible without the original bytes and would falsify evidence.

options.name: Preserve old contract and add replacement reviews
options.correctness: Retains the historical record and explicitly distinguishes missing old evidence from newly generated replacement evidence.
options.complexity: Small governance-only repair plus full re-certification.
options.migration: Save the exact closed contract, add a recovery manifest and two replacement reviews, run complete Quick, then close a new repair contract.
options.rollback: Remove only the recovery artifacts and repair contract.

unknowns: The original review bytes cannot be reconstructed from hashes alone.
selected_responsibilities: The historical B12b contract remains immutable evidence of what was signed.
The B12c recovery manifest owns the disclosure and replacement evidence mapping.
The product quality loop re-certifies the unchanged product implementation.
preserved_hard_invariants: No historical SHA-256 value is rewritten or claimed for new content.
B12 Transaction/Runtime boundary and all previous architecture removals remain permanent.
cutover_strategy: Record expected-red with missing recovery artifacts, add exact prior contract and new hash-bound reviews, then run complete Quick and close independently.
acceptance_claims: Recovery artifacts are internally hash-consistent and explicitly disclose the original loss.
The B12 transaction boundary remains at a two-package lifecycle/runtime SCC.
All backend, frontend, lifecycle and Chromium gates pass.
